rules.rule_en: A phrase is a group of words which does not contain a finite verb.
A clause is a group of words which has a finite verb.
Finite verbs indicate the tense and time of actions.
A main clause is an independent clause in a sentence.
A subordinate clause is a clause dependent on a main clause in complex or compound structures.
A clause is a group of words that contains both a subject and a predicate (or a verb).
Independent Clauses (main clauses) are complete sentences; they can stand alone and express a complete thought.
Dependent Clauses (subordinate clauses) contain a subject and a predicate, but they do not express a complete thought.
A phrase is a group of words that forms a meaningful unit but is not a complete sentence; it does not have a subject or a verb.
A noun phrase is a group of words made up of a noun and its modifiers.
A verb phrase is a group of words made up of a verb, helping verbs, and modifiers.
An adjective clause describes or gives more information about a noun—tells us which one, what kind, or how many.
An adverb clause describes or gives more information about the verb—tells us when, where, how, to what extent, or under what condition something is happening.
A noun clause takes the place of a noun in the sentence.
A Prepositional Phrase is a group of words that begin with a preposition and help to explain the relationship between two things.
A Phrase is a group of words without a finite verb.
A Clause is a group of words which consists of a finite verb.
Adjective Phrase: A group of words that does the work of an adjective by describing a noun.
Adverb Phrase: A phrase which functions as an adverb and supplies information about the action.
Noun Phrase: A phrase which acts as a noun.
Adverb Clause: Modifies the verb by providing details about the action (such as time).
Noun Clause: A clause that functions as a noun in the sentence.
Adjective Clause: Acts as an adjective and describes a noun.

examples.note_en: Contains subject and predicate but does not express a complete thought.

examples.input_en: Kalpana wants to buy a phone, but she does not have enough money.
If you don't study well, you won't pass the exam.
examples.output_en: Dependent Clause (If you don't study well) + Independent Clause (you won't pass the exam)

examples.input_en: The red umbrella was blown away in the wind.
examples.note_en: Example of a noun phrase acting as a group of words with a noun and its modifiers.

examples.input_en: The book that I left on the bus belongs to Mr. Baskar.
examples.output_en: that I left on the bus (Adjective Clause)

examples.input_en: She was happy because her father gave her a watch.
examples.output_en: because her father gave her a watch (Adverb Clause)
examples.note_en: Provides information about the verb/state of being.

examples.input_en: This is the best route that I know.
examples.note_en: Clause acting in place of a noun.

examples.input_en: The present inside the big box is mine.
examples.note_en: The phrase begins with the preposition 'inside' and describes 'the present'.

examples.input_en: Having completed the work, the boy went out to play.
examples.note_en: Phrase: does not contain a finite verb.

examples.input_en: After the boy had completed the work, he went out to play.
examples.output_en: After the boy had completed the work

examples.input_en: We bought chairs made of wood for our auditorium.
the doctors rushed there in a hurried manner.
A boy of class X became the house captain.
examples.note_en: Acts as the subject (noun) of the sentence.

examples.input_en: The students were sitting quietly in the classroom until the teacher arrived.
examples.note_en: Describes the time of the action.

examples.input_en: Whoever wins the contest will get a prize.
examples.note_en: The clause acts as the subject (noun) of the sentence.

examples.input_en: I went to the place where I was born.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: Texting on his phone, the man swerved into a ditch.
It isn’t necessary to cram all night if you have studied a little each day.
worked_exercises.answer_en: if you have studied a little each day (Dependent Clause)

worked_exercises.prompt_en: We climbed up the hill to enjoy the view.
I enjoy painting during my holidays.
Whether he attends the party or not, I have decided to go.
worked_exercises.answer_en: Whether he attends the party or not (Dependent Clause)

worked_exercises.prompt_en: I will stop playing the drums when you go to sleep.
worked_exercises.answer_en: when you go to sleep (Dependent Clause)

worked_exercises.prompt_en: 1. The girl in blue saree is my sister.
2. Kohli hopes to win the trophy.
worked_exercises.answer_en: to win the trophy - Noun phrase

worked_exercises.prompt_en: 3. The train halts at every junction.
4. I have never seen such a picture.
Ram bought a pen that doesn’t write well.
worked_exercises.answer_en: that doesn’t write well - Adjective Clause

worked_exercises.prompt_en: Come back as soon as possible.
worked_exercises.answer_en: as soon as possible - Adverb Phrase

worked_exercises.prompt_en: Most of her friends whom she had invited attended her wedding.
worked_exercises.answer_en: whom she had invited - Adjective Clause

worked_exercises.prompt_en: My brother visits my father whenever he comes to Chennai.
worked_exercises.answer_en: whenever he comes to Chennai - Adverb Clause

worked_exercises.prompt_en: Call me in case there is an emergency.
worked_exercises.answer_en: in case there is an emergency - Adverb Clause

worked_exercises.prompt_en: Until the sun sets, the old woman cannot step out of her house.
worked_exercises.answer_en: Until the sun sets - Adverb Clause

worked_exercises.prompt_en: You can go wherever you want.
